newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses after certification.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses after certification.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared earlier losses towards the close of trade on Friday, but closed down for the second day in a row.

Traders said share prices zigzagged through the session on a volatile mixture of weak U.S. markets, while the local money and foreign exchange markets were gripped by uncertainty in the run-up to Mexico's certification as a U.S. ally in the war against drugs.
The leading IPC share index closed down 10.94 points, or 0.28 percent, at 3,840.98. Trading volume was subdued at 91.2 million shares traded.

"The bourse bottomed out in line with the peso and (secondary) interest rates on the certification process. Dealers calmed down considerably," said Rodolfo Campuzano, an equity analyst at the Invex brokerage in Mexico City.
The IPC earlier reached a session low of 3,814.16 points.
"Certification certainly helped, but a tentative recovery got under way just before midday, once the forex market began to calm down," a Mexico City desk trader said.
U.S. government officials announced President Clinton had recertified Mexico in the final hour of stock trading in Mexico.
Uncertainty over the outcome of the certification process had generated considerable anxiety in Mexican markets, as decertification could have entailed economic sanctions.
The speculative onslaught against the peso on Thursday was primarily caused by those fears.
On Friday however, benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 3.4 centavos firmer at 7.9400/7.9460 per dollar.
"The problem we now have is with a volatile Dow Jones," Campuzano said.
The Dow Jones ended down 0.68 percent, or 47 points, at 6,877.74 points.
"I think we will continue to move sideways, as several factors are still making waves, but at least market feeling is not pessimistic," Campuzano added.
"The bourse had no fundamental reason to fall because 1996 earnings reports have been very good. Just watch out for the Dow," another desk trader added.
On the broad market, decliners slightly outnumbered gainers by 42 to 38, out of a total of 108 stocks traded.
Soft-drinks bottler Gemex topped the gainers' list gaining 30 centavos to 3.90 pesos after posting strong 1996 earnings earlier in the week.
Holding company Femsa was another notable gainer, up 1.60 pesos to 34.00 pesos following what analysts said was a particularly strong earnings report after the close of trade Thursday evening.
Although not among the top percentage decliners, Telmex L shares weighed heavily on the market as a whole, making up 17 percent of all shares traded.
The telecom's L shares ended off 10 centavos at 15.40 pesos.
((-- Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
